name: Peru, acclimatised
region: Lima, Arequipa, Sacred Valley, Cusco, Titicaca
tagline: Inca and pre-Inca Peru built as a slow climb: coast, 2,300 m, 2,900 m, then Cusco, the Inca Trail or Choquequirao, and Titicaca last.

access.route: Brussels→Lima via Madrid, Paris or Amsterdam (Iberia, Air France, KLM), 13–14 h; internal flights on top
London→Lima via Madrid or Amsterdam, 15 h

nightsNote: 0–5°C in the Sacred Valley and on the trek, 14°C in Lima
whyNotes: The other great Latin America option and the strongest history on the page after Mexico. July is the dry season: blue skies, cold nights, the best walking weather of the year.
fitNotes: Works if the order is respected: Lima (sea level), Arequipa (2,335 m), Sacred Valley (2,900 m) for three nights, then Cusco (3,400 m), and only after a week the Inca Trail's one pass at 4,215 m or Titicaca at 3,810 m. Still out: Lares, Salkantay and Ausangate (4,400–5,000 m) and the Colca road (4,910 m). Choquequirao is the low-altitude alternative to the Inca Trail. Crowds at Machu Picchu and in Cusco; nowhere else.

presets.name: Slow climb to the Inca Trail

blocks.name: Lima
blocks.place: Larco museum, MALI, Barranco, Huaca Pucllana
see: Museo Larco (pre-Columbian collection, the best introduction to the trip)
MALI and the historic centre: San Francisco catacombs, Plaza Mayor
Barranco at dusk, Huaca Pucllana pyramid in Miraflores
Cevichería lunch, never dinner
blocks.note: Winter garúa: grey, 16–19°C, no rain. Sea level: the easy start.

blocks.name: Arequipa
blocks.place: White sillar city at 2,335 m, Santa Catalina monastery
blocks.history: Colonial baroque, Juanita the ice maiden
see: Santa Catalina monastery (a walled town inside the city)
Museo Santuarios Andinos: Juanita
Yanahuara viewpoint and the three volcanoes
Picanterías for rocoto relleno
blocks.note: A good first altitude step at 2,335 m. The Colca canyon road crosses 4,910 m, so Colca is left out.

blocks.name: Sacred Valley base (Urubamba, Ollantaytambo)
blocks.place: Sleep at 2,900 m; Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Moray, Maras by day
see: Ollantaytambo fortress and living Inca town
Pisac ruins (3,300 m) and Sunday market
Moray terraces (3,500 m) and the Maras salt pans
Chinchero weavers
Go slowly: this is where the body adapts
blocks.note: Fly Lima→Cusco (1.5 h) and drive straight down to the valley, 1.5 h. Day trips touch 3,500 m; nights stay at 2,900 m.

blocks.name: Machu Picchu + Aguas Calientes
blocks.place: The citadel at 2,430 m; train in, overnight, early entry
see: First-entry slot (6 am) on circuit 2 for the classic view
Huayna Picchu or Machu Picchu mountain for the siblings (separate ticket)
Inca bridge walk
Machu Picchu site museum below the ruins
blocks.note: Timed tickets sell out 2–3 months ahead in July; the train is the other thing to book early.

blocks.name: Cusco, two nights
blocks.place: Qorikancha, cathedral, San Blas, Sacsayhuamán; sleep at 3,400 m after the valley
blocks.history: Inca capital under a Spanish one
see: Qorikancha sun temple and the Santo Domingo convent built on it
Cathedral, Plaza de Armas, San Blas workshops
Sacsayhuamán, Q'enqo, Tambomachay (3,700 m, short)
Museo Inka, San Pedro market, Pre-Columbian Art museum
blocks.note: Only after three nights in the valley. This is the acclimatisation step that makes the Inca Trail possible.

blocks.name: Lake Titicaca
blocks.place: Puno at 3,810 m, Uros reed islands, Taquile, Amantaní homestay
blocks.history: Tiwanaku and Inca origin myth, Sillustani tombs
see: Boat to Taquile (textile UNESCO) and a night with a family on Amantaní
Uros floating islands early, before the day boats
Sillustani chullpa towers on the way in
blocks.note: Highest sleeping altitude of the trip (3,810–3,950 m). Last stop, never first. Scenic train or 7 h bus from Cusco, 1 h flight back to Lima from Juliaca.

blocks.name: Cusco (day visit)
blocks.history: Inca capital under a Spanish one
see: Qorikancha sun temple
Cathedral and Plaza de Armas
Sacsayhuamán (3,700 m, stay short)
San Pedro market
blocks.note: 3,400 m, and 3,700 m at Sacsayhuamán. A day trip from the valley rather than an overnight is kinder to Mom. One night at most.

blocks.name: Chachapoyas + Kuélap
blocks.place: Cloud-forest highlands at 2,300 m, the walled city of Kuélap, Leymebamba mummies
see: Kuélap fortress by cable car (3,000 m)
Karajía cliff sarcophagi
Leymebamba museum (200 mummies) and the Revash tombs
Chachapoyas town, nothing touristic about it
blocks.note: Fly Lima→Jaén (1.5 h), then 4 h by road. Few visitors, lower altitude, real distance.

blocks.name: Trujillo: Chan Chan + Huaca de la Luna
blocks.place: Largest adobe city in the world, Moche temples, Huanchaco reed boats
see: Chan Chan Tschudi complex
Huaca de la Luna murals and museum
Huanchaco caballitos de totora

blocks.name: Classic Inca Trail
blocks.place: 4 days, 43 km, Dead Woman's Pass 4,215 m on day 2, into Machu Picchu by the Sun Gate
blocks.history: The Inca road itself: Runkurakay, Sayacmarca, Phuyupatamarca, Wiñay Wayna
see: Day 2: the pass at 4,215 m, up slowly from a 3,000 m camp, down to 3,600 m to sleep
Days 3–4: cloud-forest ruins, the Sun Gate at dawn
Porters carry everything; a 5-day version adds a rest day for Mom
Permits: 500 a day including staff, sold out for July by February
blocks.note: Only pass over 4,000 m on this page that is inside the ceiling. Do it after a week at altitude, choose the 5-day option, and keep the Short Inca Trail as the fallback.

blocks.name: Choquequirao trek
blocks.place: 4–5 days from Cachora: down to the Apurímac (1,500 m), up to the ruins (3,050 m), back
see: Day 1 down 1,500 m to the river camp, day 2 up to Marampata
A full day in the ruins: the llama terraces, almost no one else
Mules carry everything; a cook and guide come with the group
Return the same way, or 3 extra days through to Machu Picchu
blocks.note: Low altitude but hard legs: 1,500 m of descent then ascent each way, hot in the canyon. The siblings' kind of trek; Mom can stop at Marampata and still see the ruins.

blocks.name: Sacred Valley day walks
blocks.place: Pumamarca, the Inca quarry trail, Huchuy Qosqo from Lamay
see: Ollantaytambo to Pumamarca ruins (3 h, 3,400 m)
Inca quarry trail across the river
Huchuy Qosqo (3,650 m) with a horse option back

blocks.name: Short Inca Trail (KM 104)
blocks.place: One day, Wiñay Wayna, entry through the Sun Gate at 2,700 m
see: Chachabamba to Wiñay Wayna terraces
Intipunku (Sun Gate) arrival into Machu Picchu in the afternoon
blocks.note: The Inca Trail without the 4,215 m pass. Permits are limited; book with the Machu Picchu tickets.

blocks.name: Gocta waterfall + Kuélap valleys
see: Cocachimba to the base of Gocta (5 h round trip)
Yumbilla falls, taller and emptier
Huancas canyon viewpoint

blocks.name: Colca canyon
blocks.place: Condors at Cruz del Cóndor, terraces, canyon-floor walk
see: Cruz del Cóndor at 8 am
Canyon-floor walk to Sangalle
Chivay hot springs
blocks.note: Beautiful, and the road from Arequipa crosses the Patapampa pass at 4,910 m. Over Mom's limit; here so the choice is explicit.

notes: Dry season across the Andes: sun by day, 0–5°C nights in the valley and on the trek.
Lima is grey and 16–19°C all winter; no rain.
Machu Picchu entry tickets and the Choquequirao mules need booking 2–3 months ahead for July.
Fiestas Patrias (28–29 July) fall inside these dates: Peruvians travel, Cusco and the valley fill, prices rise for that week.

lodgingAssumption: Local B&B or Airbnb, two rooms for five, one meal out a day; shared van or hire car
